targetContext: story-045 rework; buy-and-pool UniV2 dispatcher. Base: ATokenDispatcherV2 (nonReentrant+onlyMinter+whenNotPaused on dispatch, hook.onDispatch mint-debt accrual).

findings.description: pool() executes four on-chain AMM operations at spot price. addLiquidity is called with minAmounts (amountAMin, amountBMin) hardcoded to 0 (line 413) and ALL four calls (addLiquidity 412-414, swapExactTokensForETH 448-450, swapExactETHForTokens 454-456, swapExactTokensForTokens 467-468) pass block.timestamp as the deadline — i.e. no real deadline, a tx can sit in the mempool and execute whenever a searcher includes it. Slippage IS gated at the pool() entry by caller-supplied floors (minPhusdOut, minEthOut, minPromoOut, minWbtcOut) plus a post-call minLP>=check (line 415), and pooler is authorized/trusted, so protection collapses onto the off-chain keeper picking tight floors. This is the L-06 class: single-sided / on-chain-priceless LP add relying only on off-chain keeper min params.

missingMitigations: addLiquidity inner minAmounts are 0 (bounded only indirectly by leg floors + minLP)
block.timestamp deadline = no deadline on all AMM calls
presentMitigations: caller-supplied per-leg min-out floors on the three swaps
findings.plausibility: Low/QA (MEV/sandwich, keeper-trusted; historically Low for this project)

findings.type: whole-balance native-ETH sweep + open receive footgun
findings.description: Leg B reads `uint256 ethBal = address(this).balance;` (line 453) and swaps the ENTIRE contract ETH balance into promotion via swapExactETHForTokens{value: ethBal} (line 454) — not just the ETH just unwrapped by swapExactTokensForETH. Combined with the open, unconditional `receive() external payable {}` (line 533) any pre-existing / force-sent / leftover ETH (e.g. from a prior partial Leg B) is swept into the next pool()'s promotion buy. rescueETH (line 526) is owner-only but NOT pause-gated. Value flows into the protocol-owned pool rather than to an attacker (no direct theft), so this is the L-13 / F-01-044 whole-balance-sweep class, framed on sweep + rescueETH front-run, not accidental-send.
missingMitigations: Leg B sweeps whole balance instead of the measured swap-1 delta
presentMitigations: minPromoOut floor on the ETH->promotion swap caps what a swept surplus can be sandwiched for
findings.plausibility: Low/QA (non-theft per prior INV-4 reasoning; value lands in pool, front-run window on rescueETH is the ceiling)

findings.description: rescueERC20 (519, onlyOwner), rescueETH (526, onlyOwner) and withdrawWBTC (275, onlyInsurer) are all custody/withdrawal paths that are deliberately NOT pause-gated (escape-hatch convention), and rescueERC20 can pull any ERC20 except WBTC — including resident phUSD/promotion/LP — from the contract. Owner and pooler are trusted per Law 3; this is informational centralization, not a malicious-owner vector. Flagged for completeness: the pause switch does not cover value exit.
matchedSignatures: function rescueERC20(address token, address to, uint256 amount) external onlyOwner
missingMitigations: custody exits not covered by whenNotPaused
findings.plausibility: Low/QA — likely suppressed under owner-trust (Law 3); by-design escape-hatch convention

manualReview.type: no hookTypeId guard on mint-debt hook
manualReview.description: PromotionUniV2_Eth contains NO hookTypeId guard. Mint-debt accrual is fully delegated to the base ATokenDispatcherV2.dispatch -> hook.onDispatch(minter, GROSS amount) path. The base closes the 'unwired hook = zero debt' leg of the M-04 class (constructor seeds a non-zero DefaultDispatchHook; setHook reverts on address(0)), so the classic zero-debt-because-unwired failure is guarded at the base. What is NOT guarded is hook *type/identity*: a non-zero-but-wrong hook accrues wrong/zero mint-debt with no on-dispatcher assertion. This is the L-09 surface ('no hookTypeId guard = M-04 class reborn, surface-for-triage not auto-Q08'). Route to triage; base guards make it low-confidence as an exploit.
manualReview.watchClassStatus: PARTIALLY-CLEARED (unwired leg closed at base) / L-09 surface RE-TRIGGERED

manualReview.type: gross-USDC mint-debt vs buy-and-burn phUSD decoupling
manualReview.description: The burn-half logic (phusdBurned = phusdAcquired / 2; IPhusdBurnable(phUSD).burn, lines 395-396) does NOT mint phUSD — it BUYS phUSD off the Balancer AMM in Leg A and permanently burns half (supply cut, protocol-favorable). Mint-debt accrues separately in the base hook on the GROSS dispatched USDC (line 336 / base onDispatch), while only ~60% of USDC reaches Leg A and ~30% is ultimately pooled as phUSD. This is the pre-existing DEDUP-001-suppressed decoupling (dispatcher buys phUSD off-market; mint-debt is separate accounting; per memory YS-12 the phUSD minter is immune — decoupled mint, no redeem). The rework introduces no NEW unbacked-mint path; burn is deflationary. Routed to the sanitizer to reconcile against DEDUP-001 by fingerprint rather than re-litigate.
manualReview.watchClassStatus: NOT RE-TRIGGERED by burn logic (burn is a supply cut, not a mint); gross-USDC mint-debt decoupling is the existing suppressed design

manualReview.description: pool() makes many external calls (PSM sellGem, ERC4626 deposit, Balancer swap, three UniV2 swaps, addLiquidity) and the promotion token is an arbitrary per-partner token that could implement transfer hooks (ERC777-style). Reentry surface is mitigated: pool() and dispatch() both carry the shared OZ nonReentrant lock (single _status covers the sibling set), the Balancer unlockCallback is guarded by require(msg.sender == BALANCER_VAULT) (line 492), and rescueERC20/rescueETH/withdrawWBTC are owner/insurer-gated. No unguarded state-mutating sibling shares balances with pool(). Low-confidence; recorded so the code-scanner reasoning tier confirms the shared-lock coverage rather than assuming it.

promotionToken is a per-partner arbitrary token that could be fee-on-transfer/rebasing. However the pooling step reads actual balances (promoBal = IERC20(promotionToken).balanceOf(address(this)), line 409; phusdBal likewise line 408) and the swap outputs are consumed from balance/return values, so accounting is largely balance-delta-based and self-corrects. C4 treats generic FoT as OOS unless in scope (memory: FoT permanently invalid for phlimbo-ea; check yield-claim-nft scope). Low-confidence; routed for the sanitizer/validity-checker to confirm the FoT scope boundary.
manualReview.watchClassStatus: likely OOS (generic FoT) / balance-delta reads mitigate
